reason: biome migrate eslint turns max-params (ESLint default max 3) into "useMaxParams": "error" without a max, and Biome's default is 4, so all 267 four-parameter functions stop being reported; even an explicit ["error", {"max": 3}] loses its max in the migration (same pattern as BI-2's eqeqeq ignoreNull).
evidence: biome explain useMaxParams: 'max: The maximum number of parameters allowed (default: 4)'. Repro: .eslintrc {"max-params": ["error", {"max": 3}]} -> biome migrate eslint writes "useMaxParams": "error"; function f(a, b, c, d) {} -> ESLint reports, migrated Biome not.

reason: 67 of the 78 Biome-only reports are 'The arguments variable is undeclared' for arguments used inside class constructors and methods (argparse, whatwg-url), which is always defined there; plain functions are fine. The rest: SuppressedError and AsyncIterator missing from Biome's globals (ESLint knows them via ecmaVersion latest) and one typeof value check, which ESLint's no-undef ignores by default.
evidence: Repro: class A { constructor() { this.a = arguments } m() { return arguments[0] } } -> Biome 2 reports, ESLint none (function f() { return arguments } is clean in both). The 2024 fix biome#2964 (for #2952) covered function scopes only; no tracker hit for class members.

reason: Biome reports every use of arguments, including the non-computed member access arguments.length (48 of 52), which ESLint's prefer-rest-params deliberately allows, although Biome lists the rule as the same.
evidence: Repro: function f() { return arguments.length } -> Biome 'Use the rest parameters instead of arguments', ESLint nothing. ESLint prefer-rest-params.js isNotNormalMemberAccess skips non-computed member access; its tests list 'function foo() { arguments.length; }' and 'arguments.callee' as valid. Biome page: 'Same as prefer-rest-params'. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome does not check parameters bound by destructuring, so cwd = toPath(cwd) in function ({ cwd = ... } = {}), v = ... in ([k, v]) => and minimatch's ([$0, ext = '']) are ESLint-only (11 of 12); the last one is the var-in-block scoping issue seen in noShadow (iconv-lite).
evidence: Repro: function a({ cwd = '.' } = {}) { cwd = String(cwd) } and ([k, v]) => { v = 1 } -> ESLint 2 reports, Biome 0 (plain and rest parameters are reported by both). Biome page: 'Same as no-param-reassign'; its docs show only identifier parameters. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome skips an empty block that is followed by a comment on the same line, as in eslint-scope's attach() {} // eslint-disable-line ..., although its doc exempts only blocks that contain a comment; ESLint's no-empty-function reports all 8.
evidence: Repro: class A { attach() {} // note\n detach() {} } -> ESLint reports attach and detach, Biome only detach. biome explain noEmptyBlockStatements: 'This rule ignores block statements or static blocks which contain a comment'. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome reports only the first await inside each loop and repeats it once per enclosing loop, so a second await in the same loop body is missed (postcss 336, readable-stream, find-up) and an await inside nested loops is reported twice (which 59, postcss 316).
evidence: Repro: for (const x of a) { if (x) await g(); else await h(); } -> ESLint 2 (lines 3, 4), Biome 1 (line 3); while (a()) { while (b()) { await g(); } } -> ESLint 1, Biome 2 identical diagnostics. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome treats exports as a read-only global and reports the common CommonJS idiom module.exports = exports = X (ajv, semver, whatwg-url), even in a .cjs file, where exports is the module wrapper's parameter and assigning it is legal; ESLint (CommonJS scope, exports writable) does not report.
evidence: Repro: module.exports = exports = function Ajv() {}; in x.cjs -> Biome 'A global variable should not be reassigned', ESLint (sourceType commonjs) nothing. No tracker hit (biome#11502 concerns Vue setup bindings).

reason: Biome reports the standard identifier-part class [$_\u200C\u200D\p{ID_Continue}] (js-tokens, path-to-regexp) as a joined character sequence although the ZWJ is followed by a property escape, not a character, so nothing is joined; ESLint reports a ZWJ only between two characters. The single ESLint-only report is an escaped combining mark (ajv), which ESLint checks by default (allowEscape: false).
evidence: Repro: /[$_\u200C\u200D\p{ID_Continue}]/u -> Biome 'A character class cannot match a joined character sequence', ESLint nothing; /[a\u200Db]/u -> both report. No Biome tracker hit.

reason: Biome skips async arrow functions with an expression body (p-limit's (async () => function_(...arguments_))()), because the rule returns early when the body has no statement list; ESLint's require-await reports them, and Biome reports the same arrow with a block body.
evidence: Repro: const k = async (a) => a(); -> ESLint 'Async arrow function has no await expression', Biome nothing; const g = async (a) => { return a() } -> both. Biome use_await.rs run(): if query.statements()?.is_empty() { return None }. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome misses a negated test when it is parenthesized, as in json5's (propertyString !== undefined) ? propertyString : 'null'; the same ternary without parentheses is reported by both.
evidence: Repro: const x = (p !== undefined) ? p : 'null'; -> ESLint no-negated-condition reports, Biome nothing; p !== undefined ? p : 'null' -> both. No tracker hit.
